cells.tense: You're the one holding steady right now, and your strength is moving outward to the people around you.
cells.verb: Passing strength along as it's needed.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group — the practices and language that carry what's worth keeping.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you're good at to someone who needs it — and let their honest use of it be your direction, not your permission. What comes back is not a debt but a light you can steer by: the radiance of a thing that grew to its full and now shines without your pushing.
cells.core:
You're the one holding steady right now, and your strength is moving outward to the people around you. Not performing generosity — your endurance has simply become something they can lean on, and it's landing where it's needed without you forcing it. You can feel the difference between holding and squeezing, and you're doing the first one.

The shared life around you — the words, the ways, the things you do together — is where this shows up. What you carry becomes common. That's not a small thing: it's how strength survives past the moment it's needed.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is shared and it's landing where it's needed.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a shortage that hasn't arrived — giving ahead of the need, carrying what isn't yours yet.
cells.verb: Pushing support outward before anyone has asked for it.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group — where you feel responsible for holding the whole thing together.
cells.ask: Let one thing be someone else's to handle today — not abandoned, just not yours. When you do, what comes back is a fair exchange you can feel in your body: the give and take finding its own level, no obsessive calculation, no ledger running in your head.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a shortage that hasn't arrived — giving ahead of the need, carrying what isn't yours yet. The support you offer is real, but you're offering it from a future where things fall apart unless you hold them, so your hands are always a little ahead of the moment. People can feel the grip even when the help is genuine. The weight you're under is partly the weight of what you've decided will happen.

The shared life around you becomes the place you prove you're needed, instead of the place you simply belong. You can put the load down. Nothing here falls apart when you do.
cells.sheetLine: You're giving ahead of the need, and the grip is showing.

cells.tense: You used to carry it for people, and somewhere back there you stopped letting it move.
cells.verb: Keeping strength private when it's meant to flow.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group — the table you've stopped sitting at.
cells.ask: Pick one commitment already in your life and show up to it fully, friction and all — not a new burden, just finishing what you started. What comes back is release: the ease of setting something down because it's complete, not because you collapsed.
cells.core:
You used to carry it for people, and somewhere back there you stopped letting it move. You've gone private with your strength — holding it in, not because you're hoarding it, but because the last time you put it into the shared life of a group, it didn't land the way you needed. So now you keep it close. You're still standing at a door that closed behind you.

Your endurance hasn't gone anywhere. It's just not moving between people anymore. The shared life around you feels like something you used to be part of, not something you're in.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is real, and it's not moving between people.

cells.tense: You're already supporting people around you — in how you show up, what you carry without being asked — and you talk about it like it's nothing.
cells.verb: Holding steady for others without calling it that.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group — where your steadiness has become part of the fabric.
cells.ask: Say 'I'm the one holding this' about one thing you've been calling just what's needed. What comes back is direction — a star you can actually steer by, shining because the thing you cultivated reached its full and now shows you where to go next.
cells.core:
You're already supporting people around you — in how you show up, what you carry without being asked — and you talk about it like it's nothing. The steadiness is running; the acknowledgment isn't. You'd describe yourself as just being practical, just doing what needs doing, while the people around you are quietly leaning on the thing you won't name.

The shared life around you is shaped by your hand, and you keep attributing it to circumstance. The support is yours. Saying so isn't vanity — it's the first step toward choosing where it goes next instead of letting it spend itself.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one holding this. You just haven't said so.
